A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same character-animation framework and benchmark despite the changed title. The supplied text, equations, tables, and figures are readable. V1 ends with references; v4 additionally includes Appendices A–E, which were included in the comparison.

before.justification: Tables 1–4 and Figures 8–12 report original generation results and guider ablations on TikTok, TED-talks, and Multi-Character Bench.

after.justification: V4 retains original benchmark evaluations and adds training controls, dataset analyses, evaluation-protocol experiments, and qualitative results in the appendices.

M1.justification: The three guiders, base architecture, conditioning scheme, and loss match. However, Section 4.2 changes depth-mask union to intersection and revises the compositing recurrence, while Appendix B.1 retains union and different ordering. These inconsistencies prevent determining whether the procedure changed or its documentation was being corrected. Newly detailed long-video inference alone does not establish a method change.

E1.justification: The training corpus and three quantitative benchmarks are retained. V4 extends qualitative coverage to animations with more than two characters, character rotation, and large-clothing/mask-coverage cases (Figures 15 and 21–22). The exact training-data counts supplement v1's rounded description without establishing a new corpus.

E2.justification: V4 adds AnimateAnyone† trained on the authors' noisy dataset to all three benchmark tables and Moore-AnimateAnyone to TED-talks and Multi-Character comparisons. These substantially strengthen comparison with the underlying animation approach. The ground-truth-driven MRAA*/TPSMM* numerical rows disappear from TED-talks Table 2, although their qualitative comparisons remain.

E3.justification: V4 adds a clean-TikTok training control and DisCo+ experiments varying cropping, resolution, and uninterrupted-frame sampling. Multi-Character and ablation tables additionally report LPIPS and L1. Appendix C.2 claims a DisCo sampling correction, but Table 1 retains FID-VID/FVD values 52.56/334.67 rather than Table 8's corrected-setting 47.73/312.49, leaving its application to the main comparison unresolved.

E4.justification: Beyond the retained individual-guider ablations, v4 adds an all-conditions-removed control, clean-versus-noisy training comparison, dataset noise and occlusion characterization, evaluation-protocol sensitivity experiments, and mask-coverage success/failure cases. Appendices A, B.3, and C.2 substantially broaden the questions examined.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run protocols, random seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. V4's added dataset distributions provide descriptive characterization without introducing uncertainty estimation for the method comparisons.

E6.justification: Matching existing numerical entries remain unchanged, including the method's TikTok FVD of 117.81. New TikTok control results include FVD 236.28 for noisy-trained AnimateAnyone† and 153.47 for TikTok-trained Ours*. Additional baseline and metric entries, protocol experiments, dataset distributions, and qualitative cases substantially expand the results; they do not demonstrate a same-setting performance improvement over v1.

T1.justification: The depth-map mathematics is locally revised: Equation 5 replaces union with intersection, and Equations 7–8 change the recurrence, boundary condition, and selected output. Appendix B.1 remains inconsistent with those equations. No new theorem or proof is introduced; the implicit-decoupling discussion is primarily conceptual.

C1.justification: The principal contributions remain three guiders, robustness to noisy training data, and Multi-Character Bench. V4 makes implicit decoupling an explicit central contribution and removes v1's abstract claim of over 35% improvement across two datasets and seven metrics, replacing it with a general superiority claim.

C2.justification: V4 develops explanations based on separating background motion, individual characters, and pose from texture, and explains why skeletal dilation can outperform precise segmentation masks. Appendix D newly acknowledges failures involving fine facial/hand detail, large garments, four-or-more-character scenes, and extensive position swapping, substantially qualifying applicability.

D1.justification: Appendices A–C add exact training-source counts, benchmark clip sources and timestamps, depth-map pseudocode, named preprocessing tools, and long-video inference using 16-frame windows with stride eight. V4 also reports resolution-dependent VRAM requirements and provides a project-page address. These materially expand reproducibility information without establishing changes to the retained training corpus or budget.

R1.justification: V4 adds positioning against 3D avatar approaches, including InstantAvatar and MonoHuman, and distinguishes its optical-flow use from FlowVid. It also adds newer animation/editing references and the MooreThreads implementation citation. The principal GAN/diffusion comparison framework and benchmark novelty positioning remain.

P1.justification: The title, abstract, introduction, and substantial methodology passages are rewritten around implicit decoupling. Preliminaries are consolidated, skeletal dilation receives a dedicated subsection, and the new supplement is organized into Appendices A–E. This is extensive narrative restructuring beyond scientific additions alone.

P2.justification: V4 adopts a single-column layout, reorganizes challenge illustrations, redraws workflow diagrams, and restructures comparison and ablation displays. It adds dataset-distribution plots, source and protocol tables, pseudocode, a long-video diagram, and qualitative galleries. Several earlier comparison and ablation images are retained or redisplayed rather than newly generated evidence.

improvement.justification: V4 substantially strengthens support for the central noisy-data robustness claim through same-dataset AnimateAnyone controls, a clean-data control, and quantitative dataset characterization. The appendices also address important reproducibility gaps and document concrete failure conditions absent from v1. These gains improve evidential support and applicability assessment despite unchanged existing benchmark scores. The depth-equation/pseudocode disagreement and inconsistent incorporation of the claimed DisCo sampling correction remain material weaknesses, but do not outweigh the substantial added controls and documentation.
